newsitem.title: FRANCE: Russia said weighing Mideast initiatives.
newsitem.headline: Russia said weighing Mideast initiatives.

text.p: Russia, seeking to revive its role in the Middle East, is to take new initiatives in the peace process, President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman said on Monday.
Sergei Yastrzhembsky, in Paris for Yeltsin's signing of a NATO-Russia treaty, told a news conference that Russia was doing all it could to raise its profile in the region.

"We are going to continue efforts in all directions with the United States and France, whose role has considerably increased in the Middle East, and we will take our own initiatives," he said without elaborating.
A co-sponsor of the peace process with the United States, Russia has been eclipsed by Washington in the region.
Yeltsin has received both Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in recent months but without any apparent result.
The peace process has been in crisis since Israel sent bulldozers to start a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.
Yastrzhembsky said Russia wanted to develop military exchanges with Middle East countries but without upsetting the region's military balance.
Asked about possible missile sales to Syria, he said this could upset the balance. "It is not on the negotiating table," he said.
